entries.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Production final death key pose for a 2D game animation. Attached image is the approved original DESIGN AND SCALE AUTHORITY, not a rejected animation. Redraw exactly ONE complete shadow-weasel in the following new pose: The weasel's foreknees gave way and the long body has slumped low onto its belly and left flank. Forepaws rest forward flat, wrists bent and elbows naturally folded beside the chest. Hindlegs collapse alongside the rear body, with relaxed paws visibly connected and heel joints readable. Same long back has a subtle natural spine curve into the lowered chest; preserve the original torso length and thickness. The same cream muzzle and cheek rest just above the forward paw on the ground, eyes fully closed, ears relaxed. Long thick tail has fallen behind the pelvis and lies in a lazy low C/S curve across the same floor to the right; retain its full length and thickness, no stiff arch. Preserve original brown markings, cream cheek/underside, nose, ear shapes and face proportions. No thick cylinder neck, separate collars or vanishing/amputated paws. Keep the original polished painted cartoon style, thin colored-dark contour, lighting, palette, recognizable pattern details, unchanged anatomical proportions and three-quarter camera. The pose may change occlusions and expose hidden surfaces, but the same skull, torso, limb lengths, ears, feathers and wool clusters must be identifiable. Fixed square canvas with generous transparent margins, same character physical scale as the reference. Feet/body/cheek contact one horizontal floor around 85% down the canvas. Genuine transparent alpha background. No floor artwork, cast shadow, debris, particles, effects, text, labels, grid, multiple characters, gore or animation sheet. This drawing will become actual production key-pose and part source.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Production MIDDLE COLLAPSE KEY for a 2D game death animation. Image 1 is the approved upright original design and physical-scale authority. Image 2 is the selected final death drawing, ONLY to establish the destination pose. Draw exactly ONE complete intermediate pose, no sheet: The front elbows are buckling and the chest is halfway lowered; the long back is still elevated at the rear pelvis. Front wrists and forepaws slide forward, visibly connected through bent forearms, with a soft controlled spine curve. Hind hocks are beginning to fold but their paws are still planted. Head and muzzle are lowering toward the forepaws with eyes narrowing, cheek not yet on the floor. The thick long tail has only begun to lose its upright curve, lagging behind the body. This is an unstable falling pose, not a completed relaxed prone pose. Match image 1 exactly in head dimensions, torso volume/length, limb and ear lengths, distinctive surface markings/wool clusters/feather patterns, style, lighting and palette. Keep the same three-quarter camera. Match image 2's final identity without prematurely reaching that final pose. Do not enlarge the head or flatten the torso. Fixed square canvas, generous transparent margins, same physical scale as the images, same horizontal ground plane. True transparent RGBA alpha. No floor or cast-shadow drawing, no effects, particles, gore, text, labels, grid, multiple characters or motion trails. This key will be used as an actual anatomy/occlusion source for local rig intervals and transitions.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Actual production layered anatomical source kit for a hybrid 2D death animation. Image1 is the APPROVED ORIGINAL design authority; image2 is the new final-collapse key for joint/overlap guidance. Nine separate parts in a 3 by 3 atlas: row1 complete long torso excluding head,tail,legs but including original cream belly and coherent chest/hip contours; complete original head including cream cheek/muzzle and brown nose, eyes open, WITHOUT ears or a thick neck/collar; complete thick original long curved tail with hidden root. Row2 complete near foreleg shoulder/elbow/wrist/paw; complete far foreleg; complete near hindleg hip/knee/hock/paw. Row3 complete far hindleg; complete near rounded ear; complete far rounded ear. Draw the legs as complete continuous full limbs with natural softly bent neutral anatomy and clear joint positions, not amputated pieces. All paws have the original small digits, not enormous bear feet. Keep original long torso length, head width, limb lengths and original warm-brown markings. Every attachment is individually complete, continuous, independently separated by generous transparent space, hidden contours fully painted with natural rounded fur/feather/wool, no stump cross sections, flat sliced planes, holes or outlined socket circles. Preserve exact design/texture motifs, palette, line weight, original anatomical proportions and three-quarter view. Parts are in neutral orientation for one-time anatomical registration; no animation frames. All parts should be large enough for clean extraction and full detail. True transparent RGBA alpha. No gray/white backgrounds, checkerboards, shadows, labels, text, borders, frames, grid lines, arrows, extra parts or assembled characters.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Exact production expression attachment edit. Edit ONLY the eyes of this isolated shadow-weasel head to fully closed relaxed eyelids. Preserve every other pixel and silhouette: identical skull size and shape, same wool clumps/feather spots/fur markings, same nose, beak, forehead, cheek volume and colors. Keep the head in exactly the same position and orientation on the same square transparent canvas with the same margins. No ears, horns, torso, neck, added collars or other objects. Do not recenter, zoom, resize, rotate or redraw the head design. True transparent alpha background. This actual alternate eye artwork will be precisely registered and composited into the locked head attachment, keeping the original geometry.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Actual production layered BODY POSE source atlas for this SAME shadow-weasel death action. Its head will be rendered from one separate locked attachment. Image1 is approved original design and exact body/limb size authority. Image2 is the selected middle-collapse key; image3 is the final-rest destination. Draw SIX HEADLESS BODY POSES in a clean 3-column by 2-row atlas, chronological row-major order. Remove the ENTIRE skull, cream muzzle, eyes, nose, BOTH ears and all facial fur in every cel. Draw the hidden forechest/neck base under the absent head as solid natural continuous brown/cream fur, without a thick neck cylinder, necklace or scarf. Include the long torso, all four complete connected limbs and paws, and the original thick long tail. The head removal must have no empty holes, visible sockets, flat neck cuts, extra head-shaped balls, chopped surfaces or outlined attachment rings. Keep original anatomical proportions, torso volume, limb and wing/tail lengths, recognizable fur/feather markings, original colors, painted style, line weight, lighting and same 3/4 view. Each body+appendages is anatomically connected. SAME PHYSICAL SCALE in all six cells, same horizontal floor and ample transparent margins and gutters. Do not enlarge, shrink, arbitrarily flatten or stretch any body region between cells. Action: 1 original standing long torso, low forward chest, forefeet and hindfeet supporting weight, original tail curve. 2 front elbows begin buckling and forepaws slide slightly forward, chest drops a little, hind pelvis still high. 3 foreelbows contact ground and forepaws flatten forward, chest halfway lowered, hindfeet still planted and pelvis raised. 4 chest rests on floor, knees/hocks folding and pelvis lowering, tail still lagging above the rear body. 5 same long torso has slumped on belly/left flank, forepaws forward flat and hindlegs folded beside belly, tail partly sagged behind pelvis. 6 same FINAL CORE torso/limbs as5, with only the thick tail finally coming to rest in a low C/S curve on the floor behind the pelvis. Keep torso length and thickness identical. These are actual production body cels. True transparent RGBA background. No head/eyes/ears/horns/face, cast shadow, floor artwork, background glow, gray gradient, labels, text, grid lines, borders, loose pieces, duplicated limbs, gore or effects.
